title: Separable elements in a geometrically irreducible extension
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Then $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if every element of $K$ that is separably algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] belongs to $k$.

proof.text: Assume $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible, and let $\alpha\in K$ be separably algebraic over $k$. Let $K_s\subseteq K$ be the separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]: a subfield of $K$ containing $k$, separable algebraic over $k$. It contains $\alpha$, hence contains the subfield $k'=k(\alpha)$ generated by $k$ and $\alpha$, so every element of $k'$ is separable algebraic over $k$. Since $\alpha$ is algebraic over $k$, $k'/k$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis]. Thus $k'$ is a finite separable intermediate field of $K/k$. The inclusion $k'\to K$ is an injective homomorphism of $k$-algebras, so by [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-subalgebra-colimit] (its clause (1), with $A=k'$, $S=K$), $k'/k$ is geometrically irreducible.

Let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. The finite extension $k'/k$ is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every finitely generated subextension $K'\subseteq k'$ is algebraic over $k$, so the empty family is a transcendence basis of $K'/k$, and $K'/k$ is separable algebraic by Step 1. By [lem-pc-separable-tensor-algebraic-closure], $k'\otimes_k\bar k$ is a product of one copy of $\bar k$ for each $k$-embedding of $k'$ into $\bar k$, and the number of factors is $[k':k]\ge1$. The base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_k\bar k)$, which is irreducible by Step 1. A product of $n\ge2$ nonzero rings has a nontrivial idempotent $e$, and $D(e)$, $D(1-e)$ are disjoint nonempty opens of its spectrum; so this product has one factor. Therefore $[k':k]=1$, the $k$-line $k'$ containing $1$ equals $k$, and $\alpha\in k$.

proof.text: Conversely, assume every element of $K$ separably algebraic over $k$ belongs to $k$. Let $k'\subseteq K$ be the algebraic closure of $k$ in $K$ [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]: the set of elements of $K$ algebraic over $k$, a subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and algebraic over $k$. Then $k'$ is algebraically closed in $K$. Let $\beta\in K$ be a root of a nonzero polynomial $\sum_{i=0}^d c_iT^i$ with $c_i\in k'$. The field $F=k(c_0,\ldots,c_d)\subseteq K$ is finite over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], since each $c_i$ is algebraic over $k$; $\beta$ is algebraic over $F$, so $F(\beta)/F$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis]. If $u_1,\ldots,u_a$ span $F$ over $k$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_b$ span $F(\beta)$ over $F$, the products $u_iv_j$ span $F(\beta)$ over $k$; hence $1,\beta,\ldots,\beta^{ab}$ are $k$-linearly dependent, $\beta$ is algebraic over $k$, and $\beta\in k'$. Apply [lem-zl-field-extension-algebraically-closed-geometric] to the field extension $K/k'$; it gives that $K/k'$ is geometrically irreducible.

The extension $k'/k$ is algebraic by Step 3. An element of $k'$ separable algebraic over $k$ is an element of $K$ separable algebraic over $k$, hence lies in $k$ by the hypothesis; so the separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $k'$ is exactly $k$. [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] (Tag 030K), applied to the algebraic extension $k'/k$, therefore gives: if $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then for every $x\in k'$ there is $n\ge0$ with $x^{p^n}\in k$; if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $k'=k$.

source.place: Tag 0G33 proof, implication (2) => (1), sentence 'By assumption k'/k is a purely inseparable extension', using Fields Tag 030K

proof.text: Choose the prime $p$ as the characteristic of $k$ if it is positive, and $p=2$ if it is zero. Then the inclusion $\varphi:k\to k'$ has zero kernel, and every $x\in k'$ has some $n>0$ with $x^{p^n}\in k$ and $p^nx\in k$: in characteristic $p$ by Step 4 (raising $n$ to be positive) and $p^nx=0$; in characteristic $0$ because $k'=k$. So [lem-pur-power-generated-spectrum-homeomorphism] (Tag 0BRA) applies, and for every field extension $L/k$ the map $L\to L\otimes_k k'$ induces a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_k k')\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. As $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is one point, the base change $\operatorname{Spec}(k'\otimes_k L)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ to $L$ is one point, hence irreducible; so $k'/k$ is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-transitive] to the tower $k\subseteq k'\subseteq K$. Its two hypotheses are supplied by Steps 3 and 5, so $K/k$ is geometrically irreducible.

split_report.summary: Split the Tag 0G33 equivalence into the two implications. The forward implication passes to the finite separable field generated by one element, uses the subalgebra clause of the Tag 037N node and the existing finite-separable tensor decomposition over an algebraic closure, and concludes from irreducibility of a finite product. The converse uses the algebraic-closure-in-extension criterion (Tag 037P) for the algebraic closure of k in K, the separable-first decomposition (Tag 030K) to see that this closure is purely inseparable over k, the Tag 0BRA universal-homeomorphism node to get its geometric irreducibility, and transitivity (Tag 0G30).
